grades.quote: The unused space in the last file block is called _internal fragmentation_ .
grades.reason: Defines internal fragmentation (unused space in the last block due to block-size rounding) and notes that larger blocks increase internal fragmentation but reduce external fragmentation. It does not define external fragmentation itself, so it covers only one side of the contrast.

grades.quote: Figure 6.8: Contiguous allocation leads to external fragmentation. In this example, there is no contiguous 256-MB space available for process D, even though the termination of processes A and C has freed up a total of 256 MB.
grades.reason: Only the figure caption mentions external fragmentation, as an example from contiguous memory allocation. It gives no explicit definition and says nothing about internal fragmentation, so it is limited auxiliary information.

grades.quote: This situation, where there is lots of space available but not enough grouped together in any one place, is _external fragmentation_ .
grades.reason: Gives a definition and a worked example of external fragmentation: plenty of free space, but not enough grouped together. It also shows the file rounded up to two 4-KiB blocks, which is the setting for internal fragmentation. It does not name or define internal fragmentation explicitly, so the contrast is only partly covered.
